UK Top 10 Mountain Passes for Motorcyclists

From England's brutal Hardknott Pass to Scotland's towering Bealach na Ba, these are the mountain roads that test riders and reward them with unforgettable views. Read our Lake District Passes: Difficulty Rating guide for more. Read our Top 15 UK Motorcycle Roads Ranked guide for more.

  1. Hardknott Pass — Lake District, 393m, 33% gradient. 5/5 difficulty.
  2. Bealach na Ba — Applecross, 626m, 20% gradient. 5/5.
  3. Wrynose Pass — Lake District, 393m, 25%. 4/5.
  4. Kirkstone Pass — Lake District, 454m, 20%. 3/5.
  5. Honister Pass — Lake District, 356m, 25%. 4/5.
  6. Black Mountain Pass — Brecon Beacons, 493m, 20%. 3/5.
  7. Horseshoe Pass — North Wales, 417m, 15%. 3/5.
  8. A939 Lecht Road — Cairngorms, 635m, 15%. 3/5.
  9. A686 Hartside — Pennines, 580m, 12%. 2/5.
  10. Buttertubs Pass — Yorkshire, 526m, 15%. 2/5.
keyTakeaways: Hardknott Pass tops the difficulty ranking with a brutal 33% gradient and 5/5 rating.
Bealach na Ba is the highest at 626m and also scores a maximum 5/5 for difficulty.
The Lake District supplies several of the toughest passes, including Wrynose and Honister.
Scotland's A939 Lecht Road is the highest Scottish entry at 635m.
Passes are ranked on elevation, gradient and overall difficulty for riders.

faq.q: What is the steepest mountain pass in the UK?
faq.a: Hardknott Pass in the Lake District is the steepest, with gradients reaching 33% (1-in-3) alongside tight hairpins and narrow single-track sections. It is England's toughest road and earns a full 5/5 difficulty rating. Ride it in first gear on the descents and choose a dry day for your first attempt.

faq.q: Which is the highest mountain pass on the list?
faq.a: The A939 Lecht Road in the Cairngorms is the highest at 635m, closely followed by Bealach na Ba at 626m. High passes like these are exposed to weather, collect ice and snow early, and can close in winter, so check conditions before setting off and carry warm, waterproof gear even in summer.

Difficulty combines gradient, the tightness and number of hairpins, road width and surface, and how remote and exposed the pass is. A road can be high but relatively easy, like Hartside at 2/5, or lower but brutally steep, like Hardknott at 5/5. The rating gives a quick sense of what to expect before you ride.

faq.q: Are these passes rideable for less experienced riders?
faq.a: The 2/5 and 3/5 passes such as Hartside, Buttertubs and Kirkstone suit developing riders, while the 4/5 and 5/5 passes like Hardknott, Wrynose and Bealach na Ba demand confident slow-speed control and hill-start skills. Build up gradually, ride when it is quiet, and never feel pressured to keep up with faster riders.

faq.q: When should I avoid riding UK mountain passes?
faq.a: Avoid them in winter and in poor weather, when ice, snow, standing water and fog make steep, exposed roads genuinely dangerous. Some passes close entirely in severe conditions. Even in summer, ride them early to beat tourist traffic and coaches, which struggle on the gradients and can block narrow sections.
